Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps for Acme Health

Hi Jane / Miguel,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful conversation. Below is a short recap of the pain, goals, and the recommended next steps we discussed so your team has something to share internally.

Key pain points you shared:
- High-volume inference for clinical summarization (~12B tokens/day) causing variable latency spikes during peak windows
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI within customer-controlled VPC and strict KMS controls
- Need predictable per-request latency (P95 target <= 300ms) and capacity for scheduled batch jobs overnight

Goals we heard:
- Reserved, isolated compute (dedicated GPUs) to meet throughput and compliance
- Ability to scale for bursts without data commingling
- Clear SLAs for latency and uptime, plus audit logs for compliance reviews

Recommended Redwood solution (high level):
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved pool (initial recommendation: 4 x H100-80GB equivalents; we can size to A100 equivalents if preferred) in a customer VPC with tenant isolation
- Autoscaling buffer to burst up to 8 GPUs for scheduled batch windows (overnight indexing / re-embedding)
- KV / prefix caching and request batching applied for clinical summarization workloads to reduce per-token cost and stabilize latency
- Security: KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and optional SOC2 attestation package (we'll include details)
- Target SLA: 99.9% uptime for the dedicated pool; latency SLO target P95 <= 300ms for typical 1024-token requests with warm KV cache

Attachments: I attached a capacity workbook (capacity_workbook.xlsx) with the sizing worksheet we discussed and a draft SOW (draft_sow.pdf).

Next steps we agreed:
1) Redwood to provide formal quote + SOW with committed GPUs and pricing by EOD Wed (7/15) — Marissa action
2) Acme to share any procurement paperwork and SOC2 / security questionnaire to route to our security team — Jane action
3) Schedule a 30-min procurement + security call next week to align on timelines (proposed times below)

Proposed times for call: Wed 7/15 10:00-10:30 PT or Thu 7/16 08:00-08:30 PT. Let me know which works and I will send a calendar invite.

If I missed anything or you want different sizing assumptions in the workbook, call it out and we'll update.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — great call. Adding a few technical clarifications based on what Jane said about overnight batch jobs and PHI handling.

1) Sizing notes:
- For the live clinical summarization traffic (~12B tokens/day) we recommend starting with 4 x H100-80GB equivalents reserved. If you prefer A100, that maps to roughly 8 x A100-80GB for similar usable memory footprint. The capacity_workbook.xlsx has both H100 and A100 tabs.
- Autoscale/burst: configure burst pool to allow up to +4 GPUs for scheduled jobs; scheduled scaling can be triggered via cron in your Redwood Console config.

2) Latency and caching:
- With KV prefix caching and request shaping we expect median latencies <= 120ms and P95 under 300ms for warmed sessions (1024 token context). Cold-starts will be higher; we recommend a small warm pool for low-latency critical paths.

3) Isolation & security:
- We'll deploy the dedicated runtime into your AWS account / customer VPC (VPC peering or PrivateLink options available). All keys can be managed via your KMS.
- Audit logs (request metadata, model versions, runtime metrics) can be exported to your S3/CloudWatch with retention controls.

4) Operational notes:
- Rolling upgrades are supported; we can schedule maintenance windows to avoid impacting nightly batch runs.
- We recommend a canary model rollout for any major model changes.

Attached: capacity_workbook.xlsx (filled with our initial numbers). Also attaching a short draft SLO excerpt in the draft_sow.pdf that Marissa referenced.

Let me know if you want me to swap the H100 numbers to an A100 mapping before we finalize the quote.

Cheers,

Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
